hook.text: At what step of my onboarding funnel are most users dropping off?

cta.text: For more resources on how to use Amplitude, check out the Amplitude Help Center and Community.

summary.tone: Calm, neutral, instructional academy tutorial: friendly second-person voice-over over a white, brand-blue, uncluttered look; competent and practical rather than cinematic.

signature_moments.description: Push-in on the Follow Playlist tooltip with a red outline that steps from the 80.5% drop-off line to the 90.7% from-previous-step line exactly as the VO reads each number, then a zoom back out to the full workspace.
signature_moments.why_premium: Zooming plus word-synced callouts turns a dense analytics screen into one readable number at a time, so the payoff insight lands without the viewer hunting for it.

signature_moments.description: Live change of the conversion window from 1 day to 30 minutes, with the headline dropping to 6.11% and a red callout framing the new figure as the VO explains it.
signature_moments.why_premium: Shows cause and effect inside the real product instead of describing it, which makes the abstract 'conversion window' concept concrete.

signature_moments.description: Identical animated Amplitude Academy logo lockup (circle mark, waveform draw-on, wordmark slide-out, ACADEMY label) bookends the video.
signature_moments.why_premium: A consistent, well-timed animated lockup frames an otherwise raw screen capture as part of a coherent branded series.

hook.evidence: The hook is a clear, relevant on-screen question, but it only arrives after a ~5 s logo intro, sits on a static card for ~3 s, and the VO opens with a generic definition rather than a stat, pain or demo.

clarity.evidence: Logical arc: define onboarding, show the example four-step flow diagram, build the funnel event by event, explain the conversion window, then read off the drop-off. Red callouts and the s007 zoom map the VO to the exact UI element.

ui_showcase.evidence: Real product UI is shown end to end and the s007 push-in makes the key tooltip readable, but most of the demo is a long, unzoomed full-frame capture (s006 runs ~60 s) with loading veils and small text left in.

motion_polish.evidence: Apart from the logo bookends and the s007/s008 zoom-through, the video is raw screen capture joined by hard cuts, with callouts that switch on and off with no animation, and visible chart-loading states.

sound_design.evidence: Judged from anchors plus visuals: a single SFX (chime x001 at the intro logo), no UI clicks or whooshes for zooms and callouts, a steady ~126 BPM music bed under the VO, and integrated loudness of -18.07 LUFS, which is quiet for online playback. Clean, but minimal.

vo_script_quality.evidence: Plain, accurate and well paced; defines terms ('conversion window', w183-w214), uses a concrete example (30 minutes, 6%, 80%, 90%) and a forward pointer to a follow-up video. Some filler ('you probably want to', 'let's say I want to') and the opening is generic.

brand_consistency.evidence: The matching Amplitude Academy logo lockup opens and closes the video, the title and diagram cards use the same white background, brand blue and sans type, and the product UI shares the blue. The only break is the plain red callout boxes.

works_muted.evidence: With sound off, the title question, definition card and flow diagram carry the setup and the red boxes point at the key numbers, but the how-to steps, the conversion-window explanation, the meaning of the 80%/90% figures and the CTA are voice-only. There are no captions.

overall.evidence: A competent, clear product tutorial with good VO and a smart zoom-plus-callout payoff, held back by a slow opening, long unedited capture stretches, minimal motion and sound design, and a voice-only CTA.

localization_friendliness.notes: The intro title, definition and flow-diagram cards (s002) have English text baked in and would need re-rendering. The product UI in s003-s008 is English and would need localized captures or overlays. The VO carries the instructions and the CTA, so it needs re-dubbing or subtitles. The logo bookends and the callout-box approach are language-neutral.
